problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{2n+1}{7n-5{n}^{2}}$ for $n\ge 1?$

feedback.worked_solution:
To determine whether the sequence converges or diverges, we need to determine the limit of the sequence as $n$ approaches infinity:

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{2-7{n}^{3}}{4{n}^{4}+n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $4{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{2-7{n}^{3}}{4{n}^{4}+n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{7{n}^{3}}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{4{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}+\frac{n}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{\frac{2}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{7}{n}}{4+\frac{1}{{n}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{4+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the limit exists, the sequence converges, and its limit is $0.$
